problem: Let $x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -k \\ 2k \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}k \\ -1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ Find $k$, if the distance between the vectors is $\text{d}(x,y)=2\sqrt{3}.$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the distance between $x$ and $y$ in terms of $k:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}(x,y) & =‖x-y‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{y}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{y}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{y}_{3})^{2}+({x}_{4}-{y}_{4})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3-k)^{2}+(-k-(-1))^{2}+(2k-0)^{2}+(0-(-2))^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9-6k+{k}^{2}+{k}^{2}-2k+1+4{k}^{2}+4} \\  & =\sqrt{6{k}^{2}-8k+14}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given equation  $\text{d}(x,y)=2\sqrt{3},$ we obtain an equation that we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{6{k}^{2}-8k+14} & =2\sqrt{3} \\ {(\sqrt{6{k}^{2}-8k+14})}^{2} & ={(2\sqrt{3})}^{2} \\ 6{k}^{2}-8k+14 & =12 \\ 6{k}^{2}-8k+2 & =0 \\ 3{k}^{2}-4k+1 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the quadratic formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}k & =\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a} \\  & =\frac{-(-4)\pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2}-4(3)(1)}}{2(3)} \\  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{4}}{6} \\  & =\frac{4\pm 2}{6} \\  & =\frac{2\pm 1}{3},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives $k=1$ and $k=\frac{1}{3}.$
